A - 3 month old infant with untreated CH; picture demonstrates hypotonic posture, myxedematous facies, macroglossia, and umbilical hernia. B - Same infant, close up of face, showing myxedematous facies, macroglossia, and skin mottling. C - Same infant, close up showing abdominal distension and umbilical hernia.
in_text_mentions: The typical appearance of a hypothyroid infant before the advent of newborn screening is shown in the infant in Figure 1. Features include jaundice, a puffy face and a wide posterior fontanelle with open sutures. The nasal bridge is flat and the eyes exhibit pseudohypertelorism. The mouth may be slightly open revealing macroglossia. Further examination would reveal bradycardia and a protuberant abdomen with a large umbilical hernia. Neurologic examination findings include hypotonia with delayed reflexes. Skin may be cool to touch and mottled in appearance reflecting circulatory compromise [8].

findings.label: Ectopic lingual thyroid on scintigraphy
findings.evidence: Nuclear medicine Tc-99m uptake scan showing uptake in the sublingual area with no uptake in the neck; in-text diagnosis of sublingual thyroid with hemiagenesis.

panels.rationale: Human nuclear-medicine thyroid scintigraphy (anterior/lateral Tc-99m views) with focal sublingual uptake and absent cervical thyroid uptake, in the context of congenital hypothyroidism/thyroid dysgenesis; the caption and in-text support ectopic sublingual thyroid with hemiagenesis. Not a diagram, control, other-disease panel, or third-party image. [raw subtype: sublingual thyroid with hemiagenesis]
panels.attribution_text: McHugh et al. Congenital hypothyroidism and thyroid dysgenesis: importance of newborn bloodspot screening in Ireland.. Irish journal of medical science 2026. doi:10.1007/s11845-026-04280-8. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Nuclear medicine study (8.5 MBq Technetium 99 m uptake scan) on right lateral and anterior view showing uptake in the sublingual area with no uptake in the neck
in_text_mentions: Maternal thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies and TFTs were normal. Thyroid scintigraphy was performed following intravenous injection of 99-m technetium on standard anterior and lateral views, showing an uptake in the sublingual area. There was no uptake in the neck. Thyroid ultrasound confirmed a sub-centimetre nodule of ectopic thyroid tissue sublingually, diagnosing a sublingual thyroid with hemiagenesis (Figs. 1 and 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real infant clinical photograph with color-arrow annotations demonstrating classic craniofacial features of congenital hypothyroidism/cretinism: periorbital edema with coarse puffy facies, macroglossia with tongue protrusion, sparse hair, and poor head control. Disease attribution is supported by the caption and the article title on congenital hypothyroidism. B: Real infant clinical photograph with color-arrow annotations showing classic generalized features of congenital hypothyroidism/cretinism: protruding umbilicus (umbilical hernia) on a flabby abdomen, frog-leg posture from hypotonia, and crying/irritability. Attribution is supported by the panel-specific caption and the congenital hypothyroidism article title.
